snapshot.thesis: The Seahawks no longer have their advantage in knowing what the Patriots will call. Campbell is healthy, and New England now knows that he was giving away the plays. Furthermore, the Seahawks lost Kubiak, meaning the offense will have to adjust. Given that Maye has better weapons and upgraded blocking, the Patriots look like the right play in this game at first glance. In fact, I don't hate the idea of taking the Patriots in the first half. However, the Seahawks have a huge edge elsewhere. This is a night game, and East Coast teams have severe issues playing on the West Coast at night, especially in the second half when they become exhausted. Circadian rhythms are real, like it or not, and the Seahawks have a huge edge for that reason. This really benefited them last year against the Texans, and it figures to be a nice advantage for them in this contest. However, I don't see much of an edge with the -3.5, so I'm going to take the Seahawks for a small bet. But, like I said, I think the Patriots could be the play in the first half. Our Week 1 NFL Picks will be posted all day Tuesday. Follow @walterfootball for updates.

away: The Seahawks had a huge advantage over the Patriots on the defensive side of the ball in the Super Bowl. Head coach Mike Macdonald revealed it afterward. The team had a tell on left tackle Will Campbell, whose stance identified whether the Patriots were going to run or throw. Campbell was injured, so he had to line up awkwardly at times, and the Seahawks knew exactly what the Patriots were going to do. Campbell is healthy now, so that won't be a factor. In fact, the Patriots' offensive line as a whole is better. With Campbell's improved health, as well as the additions of a rookie right tackle taken in the first round and Alijah Vera-Tucker, the Patriots will be more equipped to protect Drake Maye, who took six sacks in the Super Bowl. Maye also has much better weapons at his disposal this year. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs are big upgrades over what Maye possessed last year, and despite that, Maye was the best downfield thrower in the NFL in 2025. Maye should be even better this year, beginning with this game. However, Seattle has a great pass rush and a talented secondary, so this will be one of Maye's toughest matchups all year. I don't see the Patriots running very well either.
home: Seattle's offense didn't have much better success than the Patriots' offense in the first half of last year's Super Bowl. However, the Seahawks dominated in the second half on both sides of the ball, thanks to their running game propelling their offense. Kenneth Walker was named Super Bowl MVP despite not scoring a touchdown - one of the bad beats listed in my book, by the way - and I don't see why Seattle wouldn't do great on the ground again. The Seahawks lost Walker but drafted Jadarian Price with the final pick in the opening round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Price was stuck behind Jeremiyah Love at Notre Dame, but he's extremely talented and would have been taken earlier in the draft had he been able to start on that team. The Patriots are light up front, so I don't see them being much better against the run this year. Price should play very well, setting up easier throwing opportunities for Sam Darnold, who struggled in the Super Bowl. Given Darnold's favorable conditions, he should be fine in this game. There is some cause for concern, however. The Seahawks lost their great offensive coordinator, Klint Kubiak, who is now head coach of the Raiders. That's one of the main things I'm eager to see in this game: How will Seattle's offense adjust, especially against a defensive mastermind like Mike Vrabel?
